name: headroom
description: Local context-compression proxy + storage codec. Generation may run compressed; judgment never does.
upstream_note: PyPI metadata for headroom-ai still records the pre-rename path github.com/chopratejas/headroom, which now 301-redirects here. The canonical repo above is what was verified; the redirect is recorded so a reader who checks PyPI and sees a different URL knows why.

pinned_version.pin_provenance: Resolved READ-ONLY from the PyPI JSON index (pypi.org/pypi/headroom-ai/json) on 2026-08-04. Nothing was installed, downloaded or executed to obtain it. The digest is the sdist's, because `uv tool install` resolves a different wheel per platform and a single per-platform digest would be a pin that is wrong on five machines out of six. It is therefore the SOURCE artifact digest, not the digest of whatever wheel a given machine ends up with — which is exactly why `installs_via.kind` is "upstream" and the receipt reads "deferred-upstream" rather than claiming a local verification that never happened.

permission_class_note: DUAL, and both are enforced. Headroom sits on the wire (traffic-proxy) AND encodes what hmd writes to disk (storage-codec). Declaring only the first would silently skip the round-trip fidelity check; declaring only the second would silently skip gates-read-raw. Each class contributes its own invariants and the union runs.
tier_note: `tier` is an EVIDENCE claim and `default_included` is a DISTRIBUTION fact; they are deliberately separate fields. Headroom ships in hmd's default module set, and it has NOT earned `suggested` — that tier requires a green pre-registered A/B receipt under `tier_evidence`, and the A/B has not run. Shipping something by default proves nothing about whether it helps, so the distribution decision is not allowed to launder itself into an evidence claim. If the A/B comes back red, this stays exactly as it is: available, default-included, honestly unproven, with the negative receipt published.

installs_via.note: DEPEND, DON'T CLONE. Nothing of Headroom's source is vendored into this repo and no code path here runs the fetch — it is the command an operator runs, recorded so the pin is reviewable. Absence of Headroom is a fully supported state: the codec seam falls back to plain and the wrap chain runs without the proxy hop.

wires.detail: `hmd wrap <tool>` offers the chain hmd setup -> headroom proxy -> tool. GENERATION traffic may traverse the proxy. JUDGMENT traffic may not: every verdict-producing execution goes through hmd_gate_exec (bin/lib/hmd-gate-endpoint.sh), which unsets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, the HTTP(S)/ALL/NO_PROXY pairs in both cases, and Headroom's own HEADROOM_* namespace, then pins the endpoint to the real provider. The scrub is applied at the gate-EXECUTION boundary, so it covers the whole chain rather than one client.

The MemoryCodec seam flips to the headroom backend for corpus, context-branch and session-summary payloads when the library is importable and exposes a compatible entrypoint; every other outcome lands on plain. The seam offers NO environment lever — a backend arrives by import detection or an explicit in-process register_backend() call — because a routing var is precisely how a compressing proxy reaches a judge.

non-interactive-passthrough.command: a="$(bin/heimdall-modules --json list </dev/null 2>/dev/null)"; b="$(env HEADROOM_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9 HEADROOM_PROXY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9 HEADROOM_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:9 HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:9 ALL_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:9 bin/heimdall-modules --json list </dev/null 2>/dev/null)"; [ -n "$a" ] && [ "$a" = "$b" ] && printf 'PASSTHROUGH-OK'
non-interactive-passthrough.why: A DIFFERENTIAL check, not an assertion that something ran. The same piped, non-TTY invocation is run twice — once clean, once with every Headroom routing var and the generic proxy vars exported — and the two outputs must be byte-identical. A proxy that only behaves on a TTY, or that lets ambient routing vars change hmd's non-interactive output, breaks CI silently; this goes RED the moment it does.

no-signed-traffic-routing.command:
set -u
. bin/lib/cp-consent.sh
. bin/lib/hmd-gate-endpoint.sh
CP="${HEIMDALL_DEFAULT_CP_URL%/}"
DEAD="http://127.0.0.1:9"
clean="$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 15 "$CP/readyz" 2>/dev/null || printf '000')"
if [ "$clean" != "200" ]; then printf 'NON_VERIFIED control-plane unreachable (clean probe -> %s); an unverifiable check FAILS, it never passes' "$clean"; exit 1; fi
signed="$(CP_PROBE="$CP" HEADROOM_BASE_URL="$DEAD" HEADROOM_PROXY="$DEAD" HEADROOM_PROXY_URL="$DEAD" HTTP_PROXY="$DEAD" HTTPS_PROXY="$DEAD" ALL_PROXY="$DEAD" http_proxy="$DEAD" https_proxy="$DEAD" all_proxy="$DEAD" hmd_signed_exec sh -c 'curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 15 "$CP_PROBE/readyz"' 2>/dev/null || printf '000')"
naked="$(HTTP_PROXY="$DEAD" HTTPS_PROXY="$DEAD" ALL_PROXY="$DEAD" http_proxy="$DEAD" https_proxy="$DEAD" all_proxy="$DEAD" curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 15 "$CP/readyz" 2>/dev/null || printf '000')"
kept="$(HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.corp.example:3128 hmd_signed_exec env | grep -c '^HTTPS_PROXY=')"
wired=0
for f in bin/heimdall-presence bin/heimdall-connect bin/heimdall-team; do grep -q hmd_signed_exec "$f" && wired=$((wired+1)); done
if [ "$signed" = "200" ] && [ "$naked" != "200" ] && [ "$kept" = "1" ] && [ "$wired" = "3" ]; then printf 'SIGNED-BYPASS-OK signed=%s unscrubbed=%s corp-kept=%s wired=%s' "$signed" "$naked" "$kept" "$wired"; else printf 'SIGNED-ROUTED signed=%s unscrubbed=%s corp-kept=%s wired=%s' "$signed" "$naked" "$kept" "$wired"; exit 1; fi
no-signed-traffic-routing.why: A RUNTIME DIFFERENTIAL, and it replaces a check that was INVERTED. The old command grepped the control-plane scripts for proxy-routing variables and printed BYPASS-OK when it found NONE — but a script that never MENTIONS a proxy is exactly the script that silently INHERITS an ambient one, because curl and urllib both read HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY from the environment whether or not the caller ever heard of them. Measured: `heimdall-presence beat` under a loopback rewriter delivered POST /presence to the REWRITER and zero bytes to the control plane, while the invariant printed BYPASS-OK. What runs now: a live control-plane request is made with Headroom's whole namespace AND every generic proxy var exported at a dead loopback port, routed through hmd_signed_exec (bin/lib/hmd-gate-endpoint.sh) — it must still return 200, proving the signed path stepped around the rewriter. A POSITIVE CONTROL makes the same request WITHOUT the scrub and demands it fail, so the arm above cannot pass on a machine that ignores proxy vars. A third arm demands a NON-loopback corporate proxy SURVIVES the scrub: a corporate HTTPS proxy CONNECT-tunnels TLS, cannot rewrite signed bytes, and is often an estate's only egress, so blanket-bypassing every proxy would break hmd for those operators to defend against a threat their proxy does not pose. The static grep is kept only as a secondary arm — it asserts all three signed surfaces still route through hmd_signed_exec, which is the mutation somebody would actually make. If the control plane is unreachable the check reports NON_VERIFIED and FAILS CLOSED: an unverifiable invariant is never allowed to read as a pass.

round-trip-fidelity.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
import sys, zlib
sys.path.insert(0, "bin/lib")
import memory_codec as mc

# The three payload kinds this module is wired to carry.
kinds = {
    "corpus": "case corpus payload " + ("x" * 400),
    "context-branch": "context branch payload " + ("y" * 400),
    "session-summary": "session summary payload " + ("z" * 400),
}

# ARM 1 — the LIVE seam, whatever backend is active: headroom when the library is
# installed, plain when it is absent. Verifier fields must come back untouched.
for k, text in kinds.items():
    entry = {"claim": text, "summary": text, "body": text, "verdict": "PASS"}
    back = mc.decode_entry(mc.encode_entry(entry))
    assert back["claim"] == text and back["summary"] == text and back["body"] == text, k
    assert back["verdict"] == "PASS", k

# ARM 2 — the fidelity guard must BITE. A deliberately lossy backend must never
# persist a payload; it has to degrade to the literal text. This is what makes
# ARM 1 mean something instead of passing vacuously on the identity codec.
mc.register_backend("lossy-probe", lambda t: t[:-1], lambda w: w)
try:
    assert mc.backend_name() == "lossy-probe", mc.backend_name()
    for text in kinds.values():
        assert mc.encode_text(text) == text, "a lossy codec reached the store"
finally:
    mc.unregister_backend("lossy-probe")

# ARM 3 — a REAL non-plain backend round-trips byte-identically through the seam.
# zlib stands in for headroom's codec on a machine where headroom is absent, so
# the non-plain path is proven here rather than assumed.
mc.register_backend("zlib-probe",
                    lambda t: zlib.compress(t.encode("utf-8")),
                    lambda w: zlib.decompress(w).decode("utf-8"))
try:
    for text in kinds.values():
        env = mc.encode_text(text)
        assert mc.is_wire(env), "the non-plain backend produced no wire form"
        assert mc.decode_text(env) == text, "non-plain round-trip was lossy"
finally:
    mc.unregister_backend("zlib-probe")

print("ROUND-TRIP-OK backend=%s" % mc.backend_name())
PY
round-trip-fidelity.why: Three arms. ARM 1 drives the live seam over the exact payload kinds this module is wired to carry — that arm exercises Headroom itself once Headroom is installed, and the plain identity path when it is not. ARM 2 registers a deliberately LOSSY backend and demands it never persists, which is what stops ARM 1 passing vacuously. ARM 3 registers a real reversible codec so the non-plain path is proven even on a machine where Headroom is absent. A codec that loses a byte loses a receipt, and a receipt that cannot be re-verified is indistinguishable from a claim nobody checked.

plain-fallback-when-absent.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "bin/lib")
import memory_codec as mc

# Data written before any codec existed must still read back, unchanged.
lit = "literal text written before any codec existed"
assert mc.decode_text(lit) == lit
entry = {"claim": "plain claim", "verdict": "PASS", "reason": "unchanged"}
assert mc.decode_entry(entry) == entry

# Absence is a SUPPORTED STATE, never an error: status must answer, not raise.
st = mc.status()
assert isinstance(st["available"], bool)
assert st["backend"] == "plain" or st["available"] is True
print("PLAIN-FALLBACK-OK backend=%s available=%s" % (st["backend"], st["available"]))
PY
plain-fallback-when-absent.why: A codec that turns its own absence into an error has converted an optional module into a hard dependency. Install can fail — no uv, no network, the wrong Python — and an operator may opt out outright; in every one of those cases hmd must keep working and previously-plain data must keep reading. This runs green on a machine with no Headroom, which is the live case here.

consent_waived_reason: Headroom ships as part of hmd. That is a DISTRIBUTION decision taken by the maintainer, so the add path discloses what Headroom does and does not stop to ask for approval. The waiver is recorded HERE, on this one module, and deliberately NOT as `consent_required: false` on modules/_classes/traffic-proxy.json: that field governs the CLASS, so flipping it would silently disarm consent for every traffic-proxy module hmd ever ships — including ones nobody has written yet — which is a blast radius nobody chose. Consent is the ONLY thing waived. The `consent_text` below is still printed at add time, both declared class contracts still run their invariants with the module active (the judgment falsifier included), and `hmd modules remove headroom` still returns the tree byte-identically. An operator who does not want it declines with `hmd modules optout headroom`, and nothing re-installs it.
consent_text: Headroom is a local context-compression proxy. Installing it puts a process on your machine that sits between your coding tool and the model provider, reads the prompts and context on their way out, and rewrites them to be smaller. It runs locally and it is not a Heimdall service: your traffic goes to the same provider it went to before, by way of a process you own and can inspect. Heimdall's own control-plane, enrollment, team and presence traffic is never routed through it, and no call that produces a verdict — no gate, oracle, verifier or panel — ever reads compressed input, because judgment on rewritten context produces confident false greens. It is reversible: `hmd modules remove headroom` deletes the install directory and every trace of it, and `uv tool uninstall headroom-ai` removes the tool. Heimdall vendors none of its code and depends on the published package at the pin recorded in this manifest. Source and licence: https://github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom (Apache-2.0).
